problem: Image-goal navigation methods degrade badly when odometry/pose sensors drift, since they depend on globally consistent metric maps or absolute pose, and end-to-end policies generalize poorly.
motivation: Real robots suffer from accumulated pose drift and noisy sensors, which breaks map-based navigation. The paper observes that relative poses between nearby nodes are locally reliable, so a graph built only from relative poses can share and bound error.
key_idea: Build a drift-resisting topo-metric graph using only relative poses with an error-sharing mechanism, and train an RL policy to select sub-goals on this graph, leaving low-level motion to classical controllers.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that representing the map with relative poses distributes drift error across the graph, and that combining image correlation with topological layout in the graph policy improves efficiency. The modular design with classical low-level control is said to aid stability and generalization.
method: Drift-resisting topo-metric graph: nodes and edges store only relative poses, used for mapping and localization of the robot
Error-sharing mechanism: spreads accumulated drift across the graph representation to reduce its effect
RL graph policy: selects sub-goal nodes on the graph using image correlation with the goal and topological layout features
Modular system: classical controllers handle low-level motion planning toward the selected sub-goal

setting.backbone: RL graph-based sub-goal policy (details not given in abstract) plus classical low-level controllers
setting.training_data: not stated in abstract (RL training in simulation presumably)
setting.observation: RGB-D images with noisy odometry (relative poses)
setting.action_space: sub-goal node selection on graph; low-level motion by classical controller
